styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Mughal mosques, forts and the walled city.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Street food, nihari and Anarkali bazaars.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Empires, tombs and the road to independence.

stays.why: Central, modern and full of restaurants and cafés; easy app rides to the Old City.
Walk to Badshahi Mosque, Lahore Fort and Delhi Gate; simple guesthouses, atmospheric but noisy.
Shopping and food on the doorstep; busy round the clock and good value.
Near museums and colonial-era buildings; a short ride to the Old City.

food: Try nihari for breakfast or lunch, plus haleem, karahi and fresh naan from the tandoor.
Food streets: Gawalmandi and MM Alam Road are the classic picks; go hungry and share plates.
Street snacks: samosas, pakoras, gol gappay and jalebi. Choose busy stalls with high turnover.
Lassi and kulfi cool you down in summer; ask for less sugar if you prefer.
Tap water is not for drinking. Stick to bottled or filtered water and skip ice you are unsure about.
more_time: Add a day for the Shalimar Gardens and the Jahangir and Nur Jahan tombs on the east side.
Cross to Wagah for the evening border ceremony; check timings on the day and go early.
History fans can swap a shopping afternoon for the Lahore Museum and the Minar-e-Pakistan grounds.

recommend.why: Two nights cover the Old City, the food streets and a museum or garden; add a night for Wagah and Shalimar.

month_notes: January: cool and dry, highs near 17°C. Pack a jacket for evenings.
February: mild and pleasant, around 22°C by day. Good for walking the Old City.
March: warming to 27°C; comfortable sightseeing weather.
April: hot at 34°C. Do outdoor sights early morning.
May: very hot, highs near 38°C. Plan indoor afternoons.
June: hottest month, around 39°C. Drink water and avoid midday sun.
July: monsoon starts; about 17 rain days and humid nights.
August: still rainy and muggy, highs near 34°C. Carry an umbrella.
September: rain eases; hot and humid but improving.
October: drier and cooler at 32°C; a good shoulder month.
November: mild and dry, around 26°C. Excellent for sightseeing.
December: cool and dry, highs near 20°C. Bring a warm layer.

climate_guide.summary: Hot semi-arid climate with a short cool winter and a hot, humid monsoon summer.

items.title: Best time: November to March
items.text: Mild days around 17–27°C and cool nights. Ideal for the Old City and food streets.

items.title: Very hot April to June
items.text: Highs of 34–39°C. Sightsee at sunrise and rest indoors in the afternoon.

items.title: Monsoon in July and August
items.text: About 16–17 rain days each month and muggy nights. Expect short heavy showers.

items.title: Humid summer nights
items.text: Lows stay near 26–27°C in July and August, so evenings stay warm.

items.title: Little rain in winter
items.text: Only a few rain days from October to December; an umbrella is rarely needed.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light cotton clothes, a hat and sunscreen; a light jacket for winter nights; modest dress for mosques.

transit.best: Ride apps or auto-rickshaws for most trips; the metro and Metro Bus for cheap cross-city runs.

modes.text: Orange Line runs 26 stations; cheap and air-conditioned.
Metro Bus (BRT) has 27 stations from Gajjumata to Shahdara; fare about Rs 20.
Careem, InDrive and Uber work in Lahore. Street taxis are rare, so book by app or phone.
Auto-rickshaws and qingqis are the cheapest option; agree the fare first.
Not a practical option for most visitors; use apps and the metro instead.
Walking suits the Old City; distances elsewhere are long and hot.
